<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Details of the Adam Optimizer and Gradient Rescaling</h2>

<div id="A4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we provide the detailed formulation of the Adam optimizer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kingma and Ba, 2015</a>)</cite> used in fine-tuning Large Language Models (LLMs) and discuss how its second-moment statistics are utilized to approximate the optimization landscape for data selection methods like LESS <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xia et al., 2024</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<section id="A4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.1 </span>Standard Adam Update Rule</h3>

<div id="A4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell(\boldsymbol{z},\boldsymbol{\theta})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝒛</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝜽</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell(\boldsymbol{z},\boldsymbol{\theta})</annotation></semantics></math> denote the loss function for a data sample <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boldsymbol{z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝒛</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{z}</annotation></semantics></math> and model parameters <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boldsymbol{\theta}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝜽</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{\theta}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math>. At each training step <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, we compute the stochastic gradient on a mini-batch <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{B}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{B}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="A4.E18" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E18.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{g}_{t}\triangleq\frac{1}{|\mathcal{B}_{t}|}\sum_{\boldsymbol{z}\in\mathcal{B}_{t}}\nabla_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}\ell(\boldsymbol{z},\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐠</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>≜</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>𝒛</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></munder><mrow><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>𝜽</mi></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝒛</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{g}_{t}\triangleq\frac{1}{|\mathcal{B}_{t}|}\sum_{\boldsymbol{z}\in\mathcal{B}_{t}}\nabla_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}\ell(\boldsymbol{z},\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(18)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Adam estimates the first moment (mean) <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{m}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐦</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{m}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> and the second raw moment (uncentered variance) <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{v}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐯</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> of the gradients using exponential moving averages (EMA):</p>
<table id="A4.EGx3" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A4.E19"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A4.E19.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathbf{m}_{t+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐦</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathbf{m}_{t+1}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A4.E19.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\beta_{1}\mathbf{m}_{t}+(1-\beta_{1})\mathbf{g}_{t}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐦</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐠</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\beta_{1}\mathbf{m}_{t}+(1-\beta_{1})\mathbf{g}_{t},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(19)</span></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="A4.E20"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A4.E20.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathbf{v}_{t+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐯</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathbf{v}_{t+1}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A4.E20.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\beta_{2}\mathbf{v}_{t}+(1-\beta_{2})(\mathbf{g}_{t}\odot\mathbf{g}_{t})," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐯</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐠</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⊙</mo><msub><mi>𝐠</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\beta_{2}\mathbf{v}_{t}+(1-\beta_{2})(\mathbf{g}_{t}\odot\mathbf{g}_{t}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(20)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\odot" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>⊙</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\odot</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the element-wise product, and <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta_{1},\beta_{2}\in[0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta_{1},\beta_{2}\in[0,1)</annotation></semantics></math> are the decay rates (typically <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta_{1}=0.9,\beta_{2}=0.999" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.9</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.999</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta_{1}=0.9,\beta_{2}=0.999</annotation></semantics></math>). To counteract the initialization bias (since <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{m}_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐦</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{m}_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{v}_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐯</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> are initialized to zero vectors), bias-corrected estimates are computed as:</p>
<table id="A4.E21" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E21.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{m}}_{t+1}=\frac{\mathbf{m}_{t+1}}{1-\beta_{1}^{t+1}},\quad\hat{\mathbf{v}}_{t+1}=\frac{\mathbf{v}_{t+1}}{1-\beta_{2}^{t+1}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐦</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msub><mi>𝐦</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>β</mi><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐯</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msub><mi>𝐯</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{m}}_{t+1}=\frac{\mathbf{m}_{t+1}}{1-\beta_{1}^{t+1}},\quad\hat{\mathbf{v}}_{t+1}=\frac{\mathbf{v}_{t+1}}{1-\beta_{2}^{t+1}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(21)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS1.p1.4" class="ltx_p">The parameters are then updated via:</p>
<table id="A4.E22" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E22.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t+1}=\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t}-\eta\cdot\frac{\hat{\mathbf{m}}_{t+1}}{\sqrt{\hat{\mathbf{v}}_{t+1}}+\epsilon}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mfrac><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐦</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><msqrt><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐯</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t+1}=\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t}-\eta\cdot\frac{\hat{\mathbf{m}}_{t+1}}{\sqrt{\hat{\mathbf{v}}_{t+1}}+\epsilon},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(22)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS1.p1.5" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>η</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta</annotation></semantics></math> is the learning rate and <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϵ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math> is a small constant for numerical stability.
Structurally, the term <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\sqrt{\hat{\mathbf{v}}_{t+1}}+\epsilon)^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msqrt><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐯</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\sqrt{\hat{\mathbf{v}}_{t+1}}+\epsilon)^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> acts as a <span id="A4.SS1.p1.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">diagonal preconditioner</span>, rescaling the gradient based on the historical curvature of the optimization landscape.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.2 </span>Toy Example: Diagonal vs. Full-Matrix Preconditioning under Coupling</h3>

<div id="A4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To complement the Adam update in Eq. (<a href="#A4.E22" title="Equation 22 ‣ D.1 Standard Adam Update Rule ‣ Appendix D Details of the Adam Optimizer and Gradient Rescaling ‣ GIST: Targeted Data Selection for Instruction Tuning via Coupled Optimization Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">22</span></a>), we visualize a 2D quadratic objective
under <em id="A4.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">non-coupled</em> (axis-aligned) versus <em id="A4.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">coupled</em> (rotated) curvature.
Consider</p>
<table id="A4.E23" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E23.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L(\boldsymbol{\theta})\;=\;\frac{1}{2}\boldsymbol{\theta}^{\top}\mathbf{H}\boldsymbol{\theta},\qquad\nabla L(\boldsymbol{\theta})\;=\;\mathbf{H}\boldsymbol{\theta}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝜽</mi><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>𝜽</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐇</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝜽</mi></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>L</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝜽</mi><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mrow><mi>𝐇</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝜽</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L(\boldsymbol{\theta})\;=\;\frac{1}{2}\boldsymbol{\theta}^{\top}\mathbf{H}\boldsymbol{\theta},\qquad\nabla L(\boldsymbol{\theta})\;=\;\mathbf{H}\boldsymbol{\theta},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(23)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">with the common initialization <math id="A4.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boldsymbol{\theta}_{0}=(-2.5,\,0)^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2.5</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn> 0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{\theta}_{0}=(-2.5,\,0)^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math>.
This choice places the start on a coordinate axis so that, in the <em id="A4.SS2.p1.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">non-coupled</em> case, the update direction
does not introduce an artificial “orbit” caused by momentum; hence the visual difference is dominated by
<em id="A4.SS2.p1.2.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">coupling</em> rather than initialization.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Two geometries (same spectrum, different orientation).</span>
We compare an axis-aligned quadratic and its rotated counterpart:</p>
<table id="A4.EGx4" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A4.E24"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><span id="A4.E24.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_markedasmath ltx_font_bold">Non-coupled (axis-aligned):</span></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A4.E24.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathbf{H}_{\text{diag}}=\mathrm{diag}(20,\,1)," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mtext>diag</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>diag</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>,</mo><mn> 1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathbf{H}_{\text{diag}}=\mathrm{diag}(20,\,1),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(24)</span></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="A4.E25"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><span id="A4.E25.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_markedasmath ltx_font_bold">Coupled (rotated):</span></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A4.E25.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathbf{H}_{\text{cpl}}=\mathbf{R}\,\mathbf{H}_{\text{diag}}\,\mathbf{R}^{\top}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mtext>cpl</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝐑</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mtext>diag</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>𝐑</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathbf{H}_{\text{cpl}}=\mathbf{R}\,\mathbf{H}_{\text{diag}}\,\mathbf{R}^{\top},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(25)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS2.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A4.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐑</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{R}</annotation></semantics></math> is a 2D rotation matrix.
Thus, both cases share the same eigenvalues (and condition number), but <math id="A4.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{H}_{\text{cpl}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mtext>cpl</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{H}_{\text{cpl}}</annotation></semantics></math> is
<em id="A4.SS2.p2.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">not diagonal in the coordinate basis</em>, yielding tilted level sets due to off-diagonal coupling.
For visualization we instantiate
<math id="A4.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{H}_{\text{cpl}}=\begin{bmatrix}10.5&amp;9.5\\
9.5&amp;10.5\end{bmatrix}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mtext>cpl</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mn>10.5</mn></mtd><mtd><mn>9.5</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn>9.5</mn></mtd><mtd><mn>10.5</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{H}_{\text{cpl}}=\begin{bmatrix}10.5&amp;9.5\\
9.5&amp;10.5\end{bmatrix}.</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Newton step (full-matrix preconditioning).</span>
Newton’s method uses the full curvature:</p>
<table id="A4.E26" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E26.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t+1}=\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t}-\eta_{\text{Newton}}\mathbf{H}^{-1}\nabla L(\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>η</mi><mtext>Newton</mtext></msub><msup><mi>𝐇</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>L</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t+1}=\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t}-\eta_{\text{Newton}}\mathbf{H}^{-1}\nabla L(\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(26)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS2.p3.2" class="ltx_p">With <math id="A4.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta_{\text{Newton}}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>η</mi><mtext>Newton</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta_{\text{Newton}}=1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla L(\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t})=\mathbf{H}\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>L</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝐇</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla L(\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t})=\mathbf{H}\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>,
Newton reaches the minimizer <math id="A4.SS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boldsymbol{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>𝟎</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{0}</annotation></semantics></math> in a single step on this quadratic, correcting both <em id="A4.SS2.p3.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">scaling</em> and <em id="A4.SS2.p3.2.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">rotation</em>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Adam (diagonal preconditioning).</span>
We run standard Adam with <math id="A4.SS2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\beta_{1},\beta_{2})=(0.9,0.999)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.9</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.999</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\beta_{1},\beta_{2})=(0.9,0.999)</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="A4.SS2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=45" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>45</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=45</annotation></semantics></math> steps,
using initial learning rate <math id="A4.SS2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta=0.25" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.25</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta=0.25</annotation></semantics></math> with a linear decay schedule.
Since Adam’s preconditioner is diagonal, it can only rescale coordinates independently and cannot represent the
off-diagonal coupling present in <math id="A4.SS2.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{H}_{\text{cpl}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mtext>cpl</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{H}_{\text{cpl}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
As a result, on the coupled landscape, Adam may drift across the narrow valley and exhibit a less direct trajectory,
whereas on the non-coupled landscape it behaves in a more stable, axis-consistent manner.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A4.F5" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<figure id="A4.F5.sf1" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18584v1/optimization_dynamics_noncoupled.svg" id="A4.F5.sf1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:476/474;" width="476" height="474"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A4.F5.sf1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">(a)</span> </span><span id="A4.F5.sf1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Non-coupled (axis-aligned) quadratic: <math id="A4.F5.sf1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{H}_{\text{diag}}=\mathrm{diag}(20,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mtext>diag</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>diag</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{H}_{\text{diag}}=\mathrm{diag}(20,1)</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></figcaption>
</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<figure id="A4.F5.sf2" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18584v1/optimization_dynamics_coupled.svg" id="A4.F5.sf2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:476/458;" width="476" height="458"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A4.F5.sf2.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">(b)</span> </span><span id="A4.F5.sf2.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Coupled (rotated) quadratic: <math id="A4.F5.sf2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{H}_{\text{cpl}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mtext>cpl</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{H}_{\text{cpl}}</annotation></semantics></math> has large off-diagonal entries.</span></figcaption>
</figure></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A4.F5.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 5</span>: </span><span id="A4.F5.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Toy 2D optimization dynamics with the same initialization <math id="A4.F5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boldsymbol{\theta}_{0}=(-2.5,0)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2.5</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{\theta}_{0}=(-2.5,0)</annotation></semantics></math>.
Newton (full-matrix) follows the direct descent direction, while Adam (diagonal) cannot express the rotation induced by coupling,
leading to a “zig-zag” trajectory on the coupled landscape.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A4.SS2.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS2.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS2.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Takeaway.</span>
This toy example highlights the key geometric distinction: <em id="A4.SS2.p5.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">full-matrix</em> curvature information can correct parameter coupling (rotation), whereas <em id="A4.SS2.p5.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">diagonal</em> preconditioning cannot, which can lead to inefficient trajectories when the optimization landscape is strongly coupled.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>Theoretical Proof</h2>

<section id="A5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.1 </span>Proof of Theorem <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 3.1 (Single-level Approximate Optimization). ‣ 3.1 A Unified Optimization View of Data Selection ‣ 3 Theoretical Analysis ‣ GIST: Targeted Data Selection for Instruction Tuning via Coupled Optimization Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a></h3>

<div id="A5.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 3.1 (Single-level Approximate Optimization). ‣ 3.1 A Unified Optimization View of Data Selection ‣ 3 Theoretical Analysis ‣ GIST: Targeted Data Selection for Instruction Tuning via Coupled Optimization Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a></span> (Single-level Approximate Optimization).
<span id="A5.SS1.p1.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Fix the current parameters <math id="A5.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝛉</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Under the first-order approximation,
Problem <a href="#Thmproblem1" title="Problem 1 (Targeted Data Selection). ‣ 2.1 Problem Definition ‣ 2 Preliminaries ‣ GIST: Targeted Data Selection for Instruction Tuning via Coupled Optimization Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> is approximately reduced to maximizing the predicted reduction in validation loss:</span></p>
<table id="A5.E27" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_table">
<tbody>
<tr id="A5.E27X" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A5.E27X.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\max_{S\subseteq\mathcal{D}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><munder><mi>max</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>⊆</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi></mrow></munder><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\max_{S\subseteq\mathcal{D}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A5.E27X.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\nabla_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{D}_{\text{val}},\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t})^{\top}\mathbf{H}_{\text{val},t}^{\dagger}\nabla_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}\mathcal{L}(S,\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>𝜽</mi></msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">val</mtext></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐇</mi><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">val</mtext><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo>†</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>𝜽</mi></msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\nabla_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{D}_{\text{val}},\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t})^{\top}\mathbf{H}_{\text{val},t}^{\dagger}\nabla_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}\mathcal{L}(S,\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="2" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equationgroup ltx_align_right">(27)</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A5.E27Xa" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A5.E27Xa.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\text{s.t.}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">s.t.</mtext><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\text{s.t.}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A5.E27Xa.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle|S|=k," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle|S|=k,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.SS1.p1.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.p1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">up to constants independent of <math id="A5.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> and higher-order terms.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS1.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A5.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">We write <math id="A5.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{val}}(\boldsymbol{\theta}):=\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{val}},\boldsymbol{\theta})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>val</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝜽</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mi>val</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>𝜽</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{val}}(\boldsymbol{\theta}):=\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{val}},\boldsymbol{\theta})</annotation></semantics></math>.
Let</span></p>
<table id="A5.E28" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A5.E28.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{g}_{\mathrm{val},t}:=\nabla_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{val}}(\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t}),\qquad\mathbf{H}_{\mathrm{val},t}:=\nabla_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{2}\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{val}}(\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐠</mi><mrow><mi>val</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>𝜽</mi></msub><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>val</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mrow><mi>val</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>𝜽</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>val</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{g}_{\mathrm{val},t}:=\nabla_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{val}}(\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t}),\qquad\mathbf{H}_{\mathrm{val},t}:=\nabla_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{2}\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{val}}(\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(28)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.SS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text">and for any subset <math id="A5.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="A5.E29" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A5.E29.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{g}_{S,t}:=\nabla_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}\mathcal{L}(S,\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐠</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>𝜽</mi></msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{g}_{S,t}:=\nabla_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}\mathcal{L}(S,\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(29)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.SS1.p2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.p2.3.1" class="ltx_text">Problem <a href="#Thmproblem1" title="Problem 1 (Targeted Data Selection). ‣ 2.1 Problem Definition ‣ 2 Preliminaries ‣ GIST: Targeted Data Selection for Instruction Tuning via Coupled Optimization Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> selects <math id="A5.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> to minimize the validation loss after training on <math id="A5.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math>,
i.e., it compares <math id="A5.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{val}}(\boldsymbol{\theta}_{S}^{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>val</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>S</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{val}}(\boldsymbol{\theta}_{S}^{*})</annotation></semantics></math> across different <math id="A5.SS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math>,
where <math id="A5.SS1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boldsymbol{\theta}_{S}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>S</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{\theta}_{S}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> is the output of the inner optimization (exact minimizer or the terminal point of a training procedure) starting from <math id="A5.SS1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">First, we approximate the intractable mapping <math id="A5.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S\mapsto\boldsymbol{\theta}_{S}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">↦</mo><msubsup><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>S</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S\mapsto\boldsymbol{\theta}_{S}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> around <math id="A5.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>
by a single geometry-aware descent step using the validation curvature:</span></p>
<table id="A5.E30" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

</table>
<p id="A5.SS1.p3.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.p3.2.1" class="ltx_text">where <math id="A5.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> is a small stepsize and <math id="A5.SS1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{H}_{\mathrm{val},t}^{\dagger}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝐇</mi><mrow><mi>val</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo>†</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{H}_{\mathrm{val},t}^{\dagger}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse.
This surrogate is a first-order approximation in the sense that it uses only first-order information of the subset loss at <math id="A5.SS1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>
and a fixed local metric at <math id="A5.SS1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">Then we assume <math id="A5.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{val}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>val</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{val}}</annotation></semantics></math> is twice continuously differentiable in a neighborhood of <math id="A5.SS1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Applying Taylor’s theorem to <math id="A5.SS1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{val}}(\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}_{S})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>val</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝜽</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>S</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{val}}(\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}_{S})</annotation></semantics></math> around <math id="A5.SS1.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> yields</span></p>

<p id="A5.SS1.p4.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.p4.2.1" class="ltx_text">where the remainder term satisfies <math id="A5.SS1.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{S}=o(\|\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}_{S}-\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t}\|^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝜽</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>S</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{S}=o(\|\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}_{S}-\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t}\|^{2})</annotation></semantics></math> as <math id="A5.SS1.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta\to 0</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>

<p id="A5.SS1.p5.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.p5.2.1" class="ltx_text">The quadratic term in (<a href="#A5.E31" title="Equation 31 ‣ Proof. ‣ E.1 Proof of Theorem ‣ Appendix E Theoretical Proof ‣ GIST: Targeted Data Selection for Instruction Tuning via Coupled Optimization Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">31</span></a>) scales as <math id="A5.SS1.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}(\eta^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>η</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}(\eta^{2})</annotation></semantics></math>:</span></p>

accent="true"><mi>𝜽</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>S</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mrow><mi>val</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝜽</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>S</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><msup><mi>η</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐠</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐇</mi><mrow><mi>val</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo>†</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mrow><mi>val</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐇</mi><mrow><mi>val</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo>†</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}(\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}_{S}-\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t})^{\top}\mathbf{H}_{\mathrm{val},t}(\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}_{S}-\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t})=\frac{\eta^{2}}{2}\,\mathbf{g}_{S,t}^{\top}\mathbf{H}_{\mathrm{val},t}^{\dagger}\mathbf{H}_{\mathrm{val},t}\mathbf{H}_{\mathrm{val},t}^{\dagger}\mathbf{g}_{S,t},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(33)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.SS1.p5.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.p5.3.1" class="ltx_text">which is <math id="A5.SS1.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}(\eta^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>η</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}(\eta^{2})</annotation></semantics></math> and hence is a higher-order term relative to the <math id="A5.SS1.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}(\eta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>η</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}(\eta)</annotation></semantics></math> linear improvement term.
(Here <math id="A5.SS1.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{H}^{\dagger}\mathbf{H}\mathbf{H}^{\dagger}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐇</mi><mo>†</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>𝐇𝐇</mi><mo>†</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{H}^{\dagger}\mathbf{H}\mathbf{H}^{\dagger}</annotation></semantics></math> is well-defined even when <math id="A5.SS1.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐇</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{H}</annotation></semantics></math> is singular.)</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text">Therefore, combining the above,</span></p>

<p id="A5.SS1.p6.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.p6.2.1" class="ltx_text">where the <math id="A5.SS1.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}(\eta^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>η</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}(\eta^{2})</annotation></semantics></math> term collects the quadratic Taylor term and the remainder.</span></p>

<div id="A5.SS1.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text">Since <math id="A5.SS1.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{val}}(\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>val</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{val}}(\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> is independent of <math id="A5.SS1.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math>,
minimizing <math id="A5.SS1.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{val}}(\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}_{S})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>val</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝜽</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>S</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{val}}(\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}_{S})</annotation></semantics></math> over <math id="A5.SS1.p7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> is, up to an <math id="A5.SS1.p7.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math>-independent constant and higher-order terms in <math id="A5.SS1.p7.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>η</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta</annotation></semantics></math>,
equivalent to maximizing the first-order predicted decrease term
<math id="A5.SS1.p7.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{g}_{\mathrm{val},t}^{\top}\mathbf{H}_{\mathrm{val},t}^{\dagger}\mathbf{g}_{S,t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐠</mi><mrow><mi>val</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐇</mi><mrow><mi>val</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo>†</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐠</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{g}_{\mathrm{val},t}^{\top}\mathbf{H}_{\mathrm{val},t}^{\dagger}\mathbf{g}_{S,t}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Formally, ignoring <math id="A5.SS1.p7.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}(\eta^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>η</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}(\eta^{2})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A5.SS1.p7.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o(\eta^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>η</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o(\eta^{2})</annotation></semantics></math> terms in (<a href="#A5.E34" title="Equation 34 ‣ Proof. ‣ E.1 Proof of Theorem ‣ Appendix E Theoretical Proof ‣ GIST: Targeted Data Selection for Instruction Tuning via Coupled Optimization Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">34</span></a>), we obtain the surrogate outer problem</span></p>

<p id="A5.SS1.p8.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.p8.1.1" class="ltx_text">Finally, because <math id="A5.SS1.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}_{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝜽</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>S</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}_{S}</annotation></semantics></math> is a first-order local surrogate of the inner solution <math id="A5.SS1.p8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boldsymbol{\theta}_{S}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>S</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{\theta}_{S}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> around <math id="A5.SS1.p8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> (Eq. (<a href="#A5.E30" title="Equation 30 ‣ Proof. ‣ E.1 Proof of Theorem ‣ Appendix E Theoretical Proof ‣ GIST: Targeted Data Selection for Instruction Tuning via Coupled Optimization Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">30</span></a>)),
this yields the claimed single-level approximation to Problem <a href="#Thmproblem1" title="Problem 1 (Targeted Data Selection). ‣ 2.1 Problem Definition ‣ 2 Preliminaries ‣ GIST: Targeted Data Selection for Instruction Tuning via Coupled Optimization Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, up to <math id="A5.SS1.p8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math>-independent constants and higher-order terms.
∎</span></p>

<section id="A5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.2 </span>Proof of Theorem <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 3.2 (LoRA induces off-diagonal curvature). ‣ 3.2 The Limitation: Diagonal Surrogates Cannot Handle Coupling ‣ 3 Theoretical Analysis ‣ GIST: Targeted Data Selection for Instruction Tuning via Coupled Optimization Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a></h3>

<div id="A5.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 3.2 (LoRA induces off-diagonal curvature). ‣ 3.2 The Limitation: Diagonal Surrogates Cannot Handle Coupling ‣ 3 Theoretical Analysis ‣ GIST: Targeted Data Selection for Instruction Tuning via Coupled Optimization Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a></span> (LoRA induces off-diagonal curvature).
<span id="A5.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="A5.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}(W)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}(W)</annotation></semantics></math> be twice differentiable and consider the LoRA parameterization <math id="A5.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W=W_{0}+BA" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>W</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W=W_{0}+BA</annotation></semantics></math>.
Let <math id="A5.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{H}_{W}=\nabla^{2}_{\mathrm{vec}(W)}\mathcal{L}(W)\big|_{W=W_{0}+BA}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mi>W</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mo>∇</mo><mrow><mi>vec</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>W</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{H}_{W}=\nabla^{2}_{\mathrm{vec}(W)}\mathcal{L}(W)\big|_{W=W_{0}+BA}</annotation></semantics></math>.
For any <math id="A5.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\in[r]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\in[r]</annotation></semantics></math> and any <math id="A5.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j_{1}\neq j_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>j</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>≠</mo><msub><mi>j</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j_{1}\neq j_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="A5.E36" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A5.E36.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\frac{\partial^{2}\mathcal{L}}{\partial A_{kj_{1}}\,\partial A_{kj_{2}}}=\big(B_{:k}\otimes e_{j_{1}}\big)^{\!\top}\,\mathbf{H}_{W}\,\big(B_{:k}\otimes e_{j_{2}}\big)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mo>∂</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>j</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>∂</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>j</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⊗</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><msub><mi>j</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></msub><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mi>W</mi></msub><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⊗</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><msub><mi>j</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></msub><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\partial^{2}\mathcal{L}}{\partial A_{kj_{1}}\,\partial A_{kj_{2}}}=\big(B_{:k}\otimes e_{j_{1}}\big)^{\!\top}\,\mathbf{H}_{W}\,\big(B_{:k}\otimes e_{j_{2}}\big),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(36)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS2.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">where <math id="A5.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="B_{:k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{:k}</annotation></semantics></math> is the <math id="A5.SS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>-th column of <math id="A5.SS2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A5.SS2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> is the standard basis vector.
In particular, whenever the <math id="A5.SS2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>W</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W</annotation></semantics></math>-space curvature couples coordinates <math id="A5.SS2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>j</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A5.SS2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>j</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> along a nonzero direction <math id="A5.SS2.p1.m13" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="B_{:k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{:k}</annotation></semantics></math>,
the LoRA-parameter Hessian contains a nonzero off-diagonal entry.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS2.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A5.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">Let <math id="A5.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w\triangleq\mathrm{vec}(W)\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{\mathrm{out}}d_{\mathrm{in}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>≜</mo><mrow><mi>vec</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>out</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>in</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w\triangleq\mathrm{vec}(W)\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{\mathrm{out}}d_{\mathrm{in}}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and define the LoRA parameters
<math id="A5.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi\triangleq(\mathrm{vec}(A),\mathrm{vec}(B))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>≜</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>vec</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>vec</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi\triangleq(\mathrm{vec}(A),\mathrm{vec}(B))</annotation></semantics></math>.
Consider the composition</span></p>
<table id="A5.E37" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(37)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.SS2.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS2.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text">Since <math id="A5.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}</annotation></semantics></math> is twice differentiable in <math id="A5.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>W</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A5.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W(\phi)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>W</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W(\phi)</annotation></semantics></math> is smooth in <math id="A5.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϕ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A5.SS2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> is twice differentiable in <math id="A5.SS2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϕ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">Let <math id="A5.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J(\phi)\triangleq\nabla_{\phi}w(\phi)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≜</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mi>w</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J(\phi)\triangleq\nabla_{\phi}w(\phi)</annotation></semantics></math> denote the Jacobian of <math id="A5.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>w</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w</annotation></semantics></math> w.r.t. <math id="A5.SS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϕ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi</annotation></semantics></math>.
A standard second-order chain rule gives the Hessian of the composition:</span></p>

<p id="A5.SS2.p3.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS2.p3.2.1" class="ltx_text">The second term involves the second derivatives of the parameterization <math id="A5.SS2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w(\phi)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w(\phi)</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">In the local quadratic setting used in the main text, <math id="A5.SS2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}(W)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}(W)</annotation></semantics></math> is approximated by a quadratic function of <math id="A5.SS2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>w</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w</annotation></semantics></math>,
so <math id="A5.SS2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla^{2}_{w}\mathcal{L}(W(\phi))=\mathbf{H}_{W}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mo>∇</mo><mi>w</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>W</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mi>W</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla^{2}_{w}\mathcal{L}(W(\phi))=\mathbf{H}_{W}</annotation></semantics></math> is constant and <math id="A5.SS2.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla_{w}\mathcal{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>w</mi></msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla_{w}\mathcal{L}</annotation></semantics></math> is affine in <math id="A5.SS2.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>w</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w</annotation></semantics></math>.
Equivalently, one may assume we analyze curvature at a point where <math id="A5.SS2.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla_{w}\mathcal{L}(W(\phi))=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>w</mi></msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>W</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla_{w}\mathcal{L}(W(\phi))=0</annotation></semantics></math>
(e.g., a local minimizer of the quadratic model), in which case the second term in (<a href="#A5.E38" title="Equation 38 ‣ Proof. ‣ E.2 Proof of Theorem ‣ Appendix E Theoretical Proof ‣ GIST: Targeted Data Selection for Instruction Tuning via Coupled Optimization Geometry" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">38</span></a>) vanishes.
Under either viewpoint, we obtain the Gauss–Newton style identity</span></p>
<table id="A5.E39" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A5.E39.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla^{2}_{\phi}f(\phi)\;=\;J(\phi)^{\top}\,\mathbf{H}_{W}\,J(\phi)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mo>∇</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mi>W</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>J</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla^{2}_{\phi}f(\phi)\;=\;J(\phi)^{\top}\,\mathbf{H}_{W}\,J(\phi).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(39)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.SS2.p4.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS2.p4.2.1" class="ltx_text">Since the theorem concerns an explicit entry of the Hessian, it suffices to compute the relevant columns of <math id="A5.SS2.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J(\phi)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J(\phi)</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS2.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS2.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text">Fix <math id="A5.SS2.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\in[r]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\in[r]</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A5.SS2.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j\in[d_{\mathrm{in}}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>in</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j\in[d_{\mathrm{in}}]</annotation></semantics></math>.
Let <math id="A5.SS2.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E^{(k,j)}\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{\mathrm{in}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>E</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>in</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E^{(k,j)}\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{\mathrm{in}}}</annotation></semantics></math> be the matrix with a <math id="A5.SS2.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> at entry <math id="A5.SS2.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(k,j)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(k,j)</annotation></semantics></math> and zeros elsewhere.
Perturbing <math id="A5.SS2.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>A</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math> by <math id="A5.SS2.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon E^{(k,j)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>E</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon E^{(k,j)}</annotation></semantics></math> yields</span></p>
<table id="A5.E40" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

<p id="A5.SS2.p5.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS2.p5.3.1" class="ltx_text">where <math id="A5.SS2.p5.m8" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="B_{:k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{:k}</annotation></semantics></math> is the <math id="A5.SS2.p5.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>-th column of <math id="A5.SS2.p5.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A5.SS2.p5.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> is the <math id="A5.SS2.p5.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>-th standard basis vector in <math id="A5.SS2.p5.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{d_{\mathrm{in}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>in</mi></msub></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{d_{\mathrm{in}}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
